target_customer: Security teams at companies using AI agents (browser agents and coding agents)
problem: Teams cannot see or control what AI agents do in browsers and on engineers' machines, and prompt injection slows enterprise adoption.
business_model: Open source extension plus B2B security product, pricing not stated (book a demo)

founders.name: Ashwin Ramachandran
education: UC San Diego, MS Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Prior employers not listed on YC page. HN post mentions a co-founder, not named in the sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Chrome extension session tracking is moderate; kernel level monitoring with eBPF, Endpoint Security and ETW across three operating systems is harder.

defensibility.rationale: The open source extension is easily copied; kernel level independent audit trail may be somewhat harder.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Enterprise browsers and agent vendors added policy controls; no acquisition of ContextFort found.

market_need_then: Agentic browsers such as Comet showed indirect prompt injection flaws in August 2025, and the founder says enterprise adoption of browser agents is slow because of that risk.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and problem focused, short lines such as 'No sandbox. No restrictions.'

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable fort metaphor but no press or community about the brand; confusable with Context.dev and similar names.

pivots.from: Copilot for construction drawing review (YC launch post)
pivots.to: Visibility and controls for AI browser agents
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred only from conflicting YC launch and company page text

pivots.to: Kernel level monitoring of coding agents
pivots.why: Not stated; the current website describes coding agents, the YC page describes browser agents

outcome_analysis: ContextFort is an active two person Summer 2025 company that appears to have moved from construction drawing review to browser agent security and now to coding agent monitoring. No primary funding or traction data was found. The repeated product change suggests searching for fit, but the outcome is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists a 500K pre-seed in September 2025 and a comparison site says 500K; no primary source. Pivot dates are not given by sources; the HN post says posted 10 months ago relative to retrieval and mentions Claude CoWork launched the day before. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found for this exact wedge, so the list is empty; Island and Prisma were only named in a 2025 article as enterprise browsers.
